model.name: claude-opus-5[1m]
model.model_note: Recorded as the actual runtime identity of the evaluating session, per #1058, not the value pinned in the agent definition frontmatter (which reads claude-opus-5). The session reports itself as 'Opus 5 (1M context)', exact model ID claude-opus-5[1m]. Scores are comparable only to other scores produced by this same evaluator. [Normalised (#667): this file recorded the runtime identity in a human-readable form while the rest of the arm uses the model id. The identity is unchanged and only its spelling was made uniform, so that a query for one evaluator returns the whole arm.]

rule_provenance.definition_match: PARTIAL MISMATCH. The launching message quoted two rules verbatim; my own loaded agent definition does not match one of them and matches the other only in part.

element8_sub4_applicability.quoted_rule: Applicable to every dataset that was processed at all, established from Element 8's collection and preprocessing fields; NOT gated on whether a repository is pointed at. The code-repository paragraph governs sub-element 3 only.
element8_sub4_applicability.my_definition_says: My loaded definition attaches the same 'Applies to' paragraph to BOTH sub-element 3 and sub-element 4, gating each on external_resources referencing a code repository or on description/purposes identifying software production as a dataset output. This is a genuine mismatch with the quoted rule.
element8_sub4_applicability.resolution: Applied the quoted rule. Immaterial to the outcome here: this record satisfies both readings, since external_resources names github.com/chorus-ai with 28 repositories AND preprocessing_strategies is populated.

element8_sub4_threshold.quoted_rule: Score 1 when the record names the processing software by name in a slot documenting processing or tooling (software_and_tools, machine_annotation_tools, any field of preprocessing_strategies including its prose, or external_resources). A name suffices; version/repo/DOI strengthen but are not required. Score 0 for (a) nothing names processing software, (b) the software named is capture/hosting/instrumentation, (c) the record names a pipeline then says its outputs are not in this release. A publisher-only pointer neither earns nor forfeits the point.
element8_sub4_threshold.my_definition_says: My loaded definition carries an earlier #1059 wording that additionally states an organisation root such as github.com/<org> 'scores 0' as a pointer, rather than the quoted 'neither earns nor forfeits'. It agrees that preprocessing tool fields are a valid carrying slot.
element8_sub4_threshold.resolution: Applied the quoted rule. Immaterial to the outcome here: the point is carried by named repositories and toolkits inside preprocessing_strategies prose, not by the organisation root, so both wordings give 1.

element4_gating.quoted_rule: Applicability is per sub-element: 1-2 open on the human-subjects condition OR a governance constraint that actually applies; 3-5 open ONLY on the human-subjects condition.
element4_gating.my_definition_says: Matches (#1060 is present in my definition in the same per-sub-element form).
element4_gating.resolution: Moot for this record: the human-subjects condition is met on Element 1 evidence, so all five sub-elements are applicable under either gate.

rule_provenance.independence: No file under data/evaluation_llm/ was opened, listed, or consulted at any point (#1061). The only inputs read were the target D4D record, my own agent definition frontmatter (to answer the definition-match question), and the rubric file hash.

issues_detected.description: human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects is true, but the record carries no informed_consent slot at all. The at_risk_populations source_caveats confirms the gap in prose: the sources 'describe no assent procedures, guardian consent, or special protections'. For a retrospective EHR dataset a waiver of consent is the expected route, and no waiver is documented either.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add informed_consent recording either the consent mechanism or the IRB waiver of consent under which retrospective records were released, or state explicitly that the sources report neither.

issues_detected.description: involves_human_subjects is true and the data are identifiable hospital records, but no IRB or ethics committee of record, approval number, or determination is documented. ethical_reviews describes the project's ethics programme (focus groups, legal-landscape analysis) rather than a review of this dataset, and says so in its own source_caveats.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add the IRB or reliance agreement of record for the multi-site extract, with approval identifier, or state that no such approval is reported in the sources.

issues_detected.description: is_deidentified is populated with a method, but no de-identification standard is named for the structured data and no identifiers-removed list is given. The record's own source_caveats states this and also states that no residual re-identification risk assessment is reported.
issues_detected.recommendation: Name the standard applied to the OMOP tables (Safe Harbor, Expert Determination, or a site-specific policy) and enumerate the identifier classes removed.

issues_detected.description: No persistent identifier of any kind. The id slot holds https://chorus4ai.org/, the project homepage, which is also the value of page. A homepage URL is neither a DOI, an RRID, nor a resolvable dataset identifier distinct from the landing page. No doi and no rrid slot is present.
issues_detected.recommendation: Mint a DOI for the released cohort or register an RRID, and give id a value distinct from the landing page.

issues_detected.description: One external resource is given without a URL scheme ('www.bridge2ai.org/chorus'), and one maintainer email is 'cmccrary@mgh.havard.edu' with an apparently misspelled domain. Both are transcription-faithful and the record flags the second in source_caveats, so this is a fidelity note rather than a fabrication.
issues_detected.recommendation: Keep the verbatim transcription, and add the corrected form beside it once confirmed with the site.

issues_detected.description: license_and_use_terms opens with the controlled-access agreement and then reports that the GitHub organisation licenses its code under MIT. Placing a code licence in the dataset licence slot invites misreading as a data licence; the record's source_caveats explicitly disclaims that reading, which contains the risk.
issues_detected.recommendation: Move the MIT statement to a software-licence slot or external_resources and leave the dataset licence field stating only that no data licence is named in the sources.

issues_detected.description: The record describes itself as 'partially released' and repeatedly distinguishes 'current released dataset' from 'anticipated final dataset', yet carries no version, version_access, or errata. A dataset that is explicitly growing is precisely the case where a version handle is needed to cite what was analysed.
issues_detected.recommendation: Assign a release identifier to the 50,000-admission snapshot and record how earlier snapshots can be referenced.

issues_detected.description: Two sources disagree on cohort size (50,000 admissions on chorus4ai.org versus over 45K unique admissions as of August 2025 in the webinar) and count imaging in different units (7,642 admissions with radiology data versus 1000 images available). The record does not silently reconcile them: it records both, states the manifest precedence rule it applied, and explains that the imaging figures are different units. This is correct handling, noted here for the reader rather than as a defect.
issues_detected.recommendation: No change. Retain the both-figures treatment.

semantic_insights: The description is unusually load-bearing: 14 contributing hospitals from a 20-centre network, five named modality standards (OMOP, DICOM, WFDB, EDF+/Persyst, OHNLP), and four quantities (50,000 admissions, 1.6 billion OMOP rows, 7,642 admissions with radiology, 23 Tb of waveforms) with the anticipated end state stated separately.

Standards use is internally coherent across four slots: the conforms_to prose, the conforms_to_standard enums, the per-collection conforms_to values in file_collections, and the five distribution_formats entries all name the same modality-to-standard pairing with no contradiction.

The NIH grant number OT2OD032701 parses correctly as an NIH activity code plus institute plus serial (OT2 / OD / 032701), and the notes carry the full application form 1OT2OD032701-01 with the RePORTER application ID, award amount and project period. The grantor named, the NIH Common Fund Bridge2AI programme, matches the award.

Controlled access is asserted consistently rather than as a slogan: confidentiality_level is restricted, every data type is stated to be under access control, clinical notes are stated to be non-exportable with only tokens leaving the site, and confidential_elements repeats the note restriction. The absence of a download_url is the correct consequence, not an omission.

The record separates the released from the planned throughout, and marks the boundary in the slot rather than in a footnote: splits, labeling_strategies, sampling_strategies and the holdout test set are each carried with a source_caveat saying the source describes an intention, not a released artefact.

Ontology terms are used where the schema expects them: instances carry B2AI_TOPIC and B2AI_SUBSTRATE CURIEs matched to the modality they describe (imaging to substrate 11, waveform and EEG to substrate 49, notes to substrate 43).

The processing chain is traceable end to end from raw_data_sources through acquisition_methods and collection_mechanisms to preprocessing_strategies, and the same named repositories recur across those slots and external_resources, so a reader can follow a modality from the hospital system to the released format.

elements.name: Dataset Discovery and Identification
elements.description: Can a user or system discover and uniquely identify this dataset?

sub_elements.name: Persistent Identifier (DOI, RRID, or URI)
sub_elements.evidence: id: https://chorus4ai.org/ ; page: https://chorus4ai.org/ ; no doi slot; no rrid slot
sub_elements.quality_note: The only identifier is the project homepage URL, duplicated as the landing page. No DOI to validate against a registrar prefix and no RRID. A homepage is not a persistent identifier for a released cohort.

sub_elements.name: Dataset Title and Description Completeness
sub_elements.evidence: title: CHoRUS Dataset; description of roughly 1,500 characters naming 14 contributing hospitals, five modality standards, 50,000 admissions, 1.6 billion OMOP rows, 7,642 admissions with radiology, 23 Tb of waveforms, the enclave arrangement and the intended uses
sub_elements.quality_note: Far past the 200-character bar and specific throughout; a reader learns what is in the dataset, how it is standardised, where it lives and what it is for.

sub_elements.name: Keywords or Tags for Searchability
sub_elements.evidence: keywords: 13 entries including critical care, OMOP Common Data Model, waveform telemetry, electroencephalography, clinical notes, Bridge2AI, social determinants of health
sub_elements.quality_note: Well past the five-keyword bar and spread across clinical domain, modality, standard and programme, so the record is findable from several directions.

sub_elements.name: Landing Page and Resources (page, hierarchical resources)
sub_elements.evidence: page: https://chorus4ai.org/ ; file_collections: five collections (OMOP structured EHR, waveform telemetry, imaging, tokenized clinical notes, EEG) each with an id, description and conforms_to
sub_elements.quality_note: Landing page present and the resource structure is genuinely hierarchical: the dataset decomposes into five typed collections, each carrying its own standard and access statement.

sub_elements.name: Hierarchical Structure (parent datasets, relationships)
sub_elements.evidence: no parent_datasets slot; no related_datasets slot
sub_elements.quality_note: No typed relationship to any other dataset is recorded, although the record names the sibling Bridge2AI data generation projects in purposes and could relate to them.

elements.name: Dataset Access and Retrieval
elements.description: Can the dataset and its associated resources be located, accessed, and downloaded?

sub_elements.name: Access Policy and IP Restrictions Defined
sub_elements.evidence: license_and_use_terms.license_terms: 'Access to the dataset is controlled and conditioned on a signed licensing agreement ... a ".edu" email address is required for dataset access'; data_governance.access_review_process describing registration, licensing agreement and provisioning
sub_elements.quality_note: The access policy is stated with its concrete preconditions, the route through the AIM-AHEAD training programme, and the named contacts for requests. Actionable as written.

sub_elements.name: Regulatory Restrictions and Confidentiality Level Specified
sub_elements.evidence: regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level: restricted; restrictions listing that every data type is under access control and that clinical notes may not leave the contributing site
sub_elements.quality_note: Sensitivity classification present with two specific, enforceable restrictions. The absence of a HIPAA or GDPR determination is stated in source_caveats rather than guessed at, which is the correct handling of an unreported fact.

sub_elements.name: Download URL or Platform Link Available
sub_elements.evidence: data_governance.access_review_process: registration form, signed licensing agreement, .edu email requirement, provisioning email once compute is granted, and access requests directed to two named institutional addresses; distribution_formats describing the Bridge2AI AI/ML for Clinical Care Collaborative Cloud enclave as the working environment
sub_elements.quality_note: No download_url slot, which is the correct consequence of controlled access rather than an omission. The sub-element accepts platform access instructions, and those are present, specific and sufficient to start a request. Flagged: the enclave itself is named but not linked.

sub_elements.name: Distribution Formats and File Types Specified
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats: five entries (OMOP Common Data Model, OHNLP, DICOM, WFDB, EDF+ and Persyst), each with notes on the metadata schema published for that modality and what remains planned
sub_elements.quality_note: Every released modality has a named format and a statement of its metadata status. The planned-versus-published distinction is carried per modality rather than asserted globally.

sub_elements.name: Related Datasets and External Resources Linked
sub_elements.evidence: external_resources: four groups covering the chorus-ai GitHub organisation with 28 repositories named individually, chorus4ai.org with its page inventory, the NIH RePORTER record at reporter.nih.gov/project-details/10472824, and the AIM-AHEAD cohort-2 webinar PDF
sub_elements.quality_note: Rich and varied external linkage, each entry annotated with what it contains. No related_datasets, which costs Element 10 sub-element 5 rather than this one.

elements.name: Data Reuse and Interoperability
elements.description: Is sufficient information provided to reuse and integrate the dataset with others?
elements.applicability_note: Datasets shared and available for reuse: CONDITION MET. distribution_formats is populated with five entries and data_governance.access_review_process describes a working access route. Sub-elements 1-4 are therefore applicable and scored.

sub_elements.name: License Terms Allow Reuse
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: distribution_formats populated with five formats; access_review_process describes a route by which external trainees obtain the data
sub_elements.evidence: license_and_use_terms.source_caveats: 'The MIT License statement is made about the GitHub software project, not about the data; the source documents do not name a license for the dataset itself'
sub_elements.quality_note: The record states plainly that no licence governs the data. Access conditions are documented and credited under Element 2, but a reuser learns nothing about what they may do with the data once inside the enclave. The honesty is the right call; the gap is real.

sub_elements.name: Data Formats Are Standardized (encoding, format)
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: same condition as above
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats: OMOP Common Data Model, OHNLP, DICOM, WFDB, EDF+ and Persyst; conforms_to_standard: [OMOP_CDM, DICOM, WFDB, OTHER]
sub_elements.quality_note: Every modality lands on a recognised community format. Character encoding is not stated, which matters little for DICOM and WFDB but would matter for the tokenized note output.

sub_elements.name: Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: same condition as above
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to: a paragraph mapping each modality to its standard, including 'the OMOP schema with extensions' for nursing flowsheets and 'the PhysioNet schema extended' for waveform metadata; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset
sub_elements.quality_note: Conformance is stated at three levels: the datasheet's own schema, the dataset's community models, and per-collection conformance inside file_collections. The extension caveats on OMOP and PhysioNet are the kind of detail an integrator needs.

sub_elements.name: Variable Metadata with Identifiers Defined
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: same condition as above
sub_elements.evidence: no variables slot; instances describe content categories (demographics, medication administration, procedures, nursing flowsheets, diagnoses) but no variable-level entries
sub_elements.quality_note: No data dictionary and no variable identifiers. Partly mitigated for a reader who knows OMOP, since the CDM defines the columns, but the record does not say which OMOP tables or CDM version are populated.

sub_elements.name: Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)
sub_elements.evidence: intended_uses: three categories (ML model development for acute and critical care, external validation of AI models, AI/ML workforce training) each with usage_notes; the external-validation entry carries a source_caveat that the holdout set is not reported as released
sub_elements.quality_note: Intended use is specific and each category explains what the data support. No prohibited_uses or discouraged_uses, which is a notable gap for identifiable critical-care data under a signed agreement.

elements.name: Ethical Use and Privacy Safeguards
elements.description: Does the dataset provide clear information about consent, privacy, and ethical oversight?
elements.applicability_note: Human-subjects condition: MET, on Element 1 evidence alone. The description opens 'a multicenter, multimodal, high-resolution, controlled-access dataset of acute and critical care hospital admissions' and refers throughout to patient admissions, ICU/PICU/NICU settings and clinical notes; keywords include 'electronic health records' and 'clinical notes'. Element 8 collection_mechanisms corroborates, describing extraction of patient records from hospital systems. Because the human-subjects condition is met, all five sub-elements are applicable under the per-sub-element gate (#1060), and the separate governance disjunct for sub-elements 1-2 is not needed here.

sub_elements.name: IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: E1 description: 'acute and critical care hospital admissions ... 50,000 patient admissions from ICU, PICU and NICU'; E1 keywords include 'electronic health records' and 'clinical notes'; E8 collection_mechanisms describes site extraction of patient records. Human-subjects condition met on external-element evidence, so the governance disjunct is not relied on.
sub_elements.evidence: ethical_reviews.review_details: 'Ethics is one of three project pillars (Ethical and Trustworthy AI). The project performs community-facing ethics focus groups to determine what data is appropriate for public sharing ... establishes a legal framework for collecting data at scale, and analyzes the existing legal and regulatory landscape'; data_governance.accountable_organization: Massachusetts General Hospital; data_governance.access_review_process; access requests directed to named institutional contacts
sub_elements.quality_note: The sub-element accepts institutional oversight and governance contacts as well as IRB approval, and both are documented concretely: an accountable organisation of record, stewardship roles, a described access review, and named governance contacts. The ethics content itself is programme-level rather than an approval for this dataset, and the record says so in source_caveats. Scored 1 on the oversight evidence; the missing IRB of record is raised as a high-severity consistency issue rather than taken twice.

sub_elements.name: Deidentification Method Described
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: same human-subjects evidence as above, from E1 description and keywords and E8 collection_mechanisms
sub_elements.evidence: is_deidentified.method: 'Tokenization of unstructured electronic health record text, transformation of data using approaches that limit re-identification, and de-identification of imaging prior to release'; deidentification_details names a privacy scan tool and a CTP-deid repository and reports 1000 images de-identified as of August 2025 with a larger cohort in process
sub_elements.quality_note: A real method per modality, with the supporting tooling named and the completion state reported. It is not a named standard: no Safe Harbor, Expert Determination or k-anonymity claim, and no identifier list. The record states that gap itself, so this is a described method short of a certified one.

sub_elements.name: Privacy Protections and Re-identification Risk Assessment
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: human-subjects condition met on E1 description and keywords and E8 collection_mechanisms. Note that the participant signal here is patient records, not the governance structure: under #1060 a governance constraint alone would not open this sub-element.
sub_elements.evidence: participant_privacy.anonymization_method: tokenization plus transformation limiting re-identification, with clinical notes retained at the contributing site; participant_privacy.reidentification_risk: 'The project states that data are transformed using approaches that limit re-identification; no quantitative residual risk is reported in the source documents'
sub_elements.quality_note: Protections are concrete and architectural: the note text never leaves the site, which is a stronger control than a redaction claim. The risk field is answered rather than left empty, and it distinguishes the project's assertion from a measurement. No quantified residual risk exists to report.

sub_elements.name: Informed Consent Obtained from Participants
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: human-subjects condition met on E1 description and keywords and E8 collection_mechanisms
sub_elements.evidence: no informed_consent slot anywhere in the record; at_risk_populations.source_caveats: the sources 'describe no assent procedures, guardian consent, or special protections'
sub_elements.quality_note: Nothing on consent, waiver of consent, or withdrawal. For retrospective hospital records the expected documentation is an IRB waiver, and neither the waiver nor its absence is recorded in a consent slot. The gap is visible only through a caveat on a different field.

sub_elements.name: Vulnerable Populations and Compensation Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: human-subjects condition met on E1 description and keywords and E8 collection_mechanisms
sub_elements.evidence: at_risk_populations.at_risk_groups_included: true with notes 'Admissions from pediatric intensive care units and neonatal intensive care units are part of the current released dataset'; human_subject_research.special_populations: 'minors and neonates are represented'
sub_elements.quality_note: The vulnerable populations present are named specifically and flagged in two slots, which is the fact a reuser most needs. The record marks it as an inference from the reported PICU and NICU admissions rather than a source statement. Protections and compensation are not documented, and the record says the sources describe none; compensation is not expected for retrospective records.

elements.name: Data Composition and Structure
elements.description: Can the dataset's structure, modality, and population be understood from metadata?

sub_elements.name: Cohort or Subpopulations Characteristics Described
sub_elements.evidence: subpopulations: three entries with subpopulation_elements_present true, identifying ICU, PICU and NICU admissions, each carrying the caveat that the 50,000 figure is reported for the three settings combined with no per-setting breakdown
sub_elements.quality_note: The care settings that partition the cohort are named and flagged as present. Thin on demographics: no age, sex, race or geography distribution, and no inclusion or exclusion criteria, which the record attributes to the sources rather than to itself.

sub_elements.name: Number of Instances or Samples Reported
sub_elements.evidence: instances counts: 50000 hospital admissions, 1600000000 OMOP rows, 7642 admissions with radiology data; waveform reported as 23 Tb with the record noting no file count is given; splits describing the planned sequestered holdout
sub_elements.quality_note: Counts are given per instance type with the unit made explicit, and the anticipated 100,000-admission end state is kept separate from the released figure. Where a count does not exist the record says so rather than inventing one.

sub_elements.name: Variable-Level Metadata and Tabular Flag
sub_elements.evidence: no variables slot; no is_tabular slot
sub_elements.quality_note: No variable descriptions, no data dictionary and no tabular indicator, despite 1.6 billion rows of structured OMOP data being the largest component. The instance notes list content categories but not columns.

sub_elements.name: Data Topics or Conditions Represented
sub_elements.evidence: instances carry data_topic CURIEs B2AI_TOPIC:9, :15, :32, :37 and data_substrate CURIEs B2AI_SUBSTRATE:11, :43, :49 matched to the modality of each instance type; description states the domain as acute and critical care illness
sub_elements.quality_note: Topics are given as ontology terms rather than free text and are correctly paired with their modality. Clinical conditions within critical care are not enumerated, so the topical resolution stops at the modality and setting level.

sub_elements.name: Data Quality Issues and Anomalies Documented
sub_elements.evidence: instances missing_information blocks pairing what is missing with why (imaging beyond about 1,000 images, because de-identification was in process; full clinical note text, because notes stay local and only tokens leave); sampling_strategies with a caveat that only intended sampling is reported, not what was applied to the released 50,000
sub_elements.quality_note: Missing data is documented where it occurs, with a stated cause, and the sampling gap is named as a gap. No anomalies slot, so outliers, artefacts and known errors within the released data are not addressed; that costs Element 9 sub-element 3 rather than this one.

elements.name: Data Provenance and Version Tracking
elements.description: Can a user determine dataset versions, update history, and provenance?
elements.applicability_note: Datasets shared and available for reuse: CONDITION MET (distribution_formats populated, documented access route). All five sub-elements applicable and scored.

sub_elements.name: Dataset Version Number Provided
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: distribution_formats populated with five formats; access_review_process describes an operating access route
sub_elements.evidence: no version slot; status: partially released
sub_elements.quality_note: No version handle at all, in a record that repeatedly contrasts the 'current released dataset' with the 'anticipated final dataset'. A reuser cannot cite which snapshot they analysed.

sub_elements.name: Version Access Methods Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: same condition as above
sub_elements.evidence: no version_access slot
sub_elements.quality_note: Nothing on retrieving an earlier state of the dataset. Given continuous accrual toward 100,000 admissions, the absence means an analysis cannot be reproduced against the data as they stood.

sub_elements.name: Change Descriptions and Errata Provided
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: same condition as above
sub_elements.evidence: no errata slot; updates.update_details describes ongoing acquisition but records no change history
sub_elements.quality_note: No changelog and no errata. The August 2025 snapshot is described but not as a distinguishable prior state with recorded differences.

sub_elements.name: Update Schedule or Frequency Indicated
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: same condition as above
sub_elements.evidence: updates.update_details: 'Data acquisition is ongoing. The current released dataset covers 50,000 patient admissions, while the anticipated final dataset is 100,000 patient admissions across 9 data modalities from 14 data contributing hospitals. Imaging de-identification for a larger cohort and EEG extraction were in process as of August 2025. Contributing sites provide regular status updates on their progress'
sub_elements.quality_note: Scored on the maintenance-plan limb of the sub-element: the growth trajectory, the target end state, the modalities still in process and the reporting rhythm are all stated, so a reuser knows the dataset is actively accruing and roughly toward what. No release cadence or versioning policy, which the record states in its own caveat and which is the weaker half of this point.

sub_elements.name: Provenance and Source Derivation Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: same condition as above
sub_elements.evidence: was_derived_from: clinical source systems at the 14 contributing hospitals, naming EHRs, PACS archives, bedside monitors with gateway/middleware and hospital EEG databases; raw_data_sources: five entries each with source_description, source_type, raw_data_format and, where relevant, access_details
sub_elements.quality_note: Provenance is traceable per modality from the hospital system through the native format to the delivered standard, including the fact that only the standardised extract, not the source record, reaches CHoRUS. No release notes, which is the one missing piece.

elements.name: Scientific Motivation and Funding Transparency
elements.description: Does the metadata clearly state why the dataset exists and who funded it?

sub_elements.name: Motivation or Purpose for Dataset Creation
sub_elements.evidence: purposes: four responses covering ML/AI applications for characterising critical illness, building a publicly available AI-ready dataset with privacy and accountability, provisioning a holdout for external validation, and coordinating best practices across Bridge2AI; addressing_gaps: three responses on the need for critical-care AI infrastructure and unified multi-modal standards
sub_elements.quality_note: Purpose and the gap it answers are stated separately and both are specific to critical care rather than generic AI-readiness language.

sub_elements.name: Primary Research Objectives or Tasks
sub_elements.evidence: tasks: characterising acute and critical care illness; predicting complications and clinical deterioration; measuring treatment response; external validation of models against a sequestered holdout
sub_elements.quality_note: Four concrete analytic tasks, each of a kind that maps onto a modelling problem. The holdout task is marked as an award-abstract statement rather than a released capability.

sub_elements.name: Funding Sources and Mechanisms Listed
sub_elements.evidence: funders.grantor: 'National Institutes of Health, Common Fund Bridge2AI program'
sub_elements.quality_note: Agency and the specific programme within it are both named, which is what distinguishes this award from any other NIH funding.

sub_elements.name: Grant IDs or Award Numbers Present
sub_elements.evidence: funders.grants.grant_number: OT2OD032701, with notes giving the RePORTER form '1OT2OD032701-01', application ID 10472824, fiscal year 2022, award amount 5880300, and a project period of 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30
sub_elements.quality_note: Format validates as NIH: activity code OT2, institute OD, serial 032701, with the applicant-type and support-year suffixes carried in the full form. Corroborated against both the project website and the RePORTER record, and the award period is temporally consistent with the August 2025 snapshot.

sub_elements.name: Creators and Acknowledgements Documented
sub_elements.evidence: creators: seven entries including a principal investigator with an id and affiliation, five named leadership members with institutions, and a consortium entry noting more than 60 members across 20 institutions; created_by: CHoRUS Consortium; maintainers and data_collectors with roles and details
sub_elements.quality_note: Attribution is layered across individuals, the consortium and the maintaining roles, and each creator entry records where the name was found, including the RePORTER spelling of the PI's name.

elements.name: Technical Transparency (Data Collection and Processing)
elements.description: Can data collection and processing steps be replicated or understood?
elements.applicability_note: Sub-elements 1-2: data collection identified (acquisition_methods and collection_mechanisms populated) AND datasets shared (distribution_formats, access route) - CONDITION MET. Sub-element 3: external_resources references a code repository - CONDITION MET, via 'https://github.com/chorus-ai ... holding 28 repositories including chorus-extract-upload, Chorus_SOP, data_acq_SOP, chorus_waveform, chorus_waveform_resources, chorus-container-apps, CHoRUSReports, privacy_scan_tool and CTP-deid'. Sub-element 4: under the rule quoted by the launching agent (#1079), applicable to every dataset that was processed at all, established from Element 8's collection and preprocessing fields, which are populated; the code-repository paragraph governs sub-element 3 only. Under my own loaded definition, which gates sub-element 4 on the same repository condition, it is applicable too, since that condition is met. Both readings give the same result. Sub-element 5: datasets shared - CONDITION MET.

sub_elements.name: Collection Mechanisms and Settings Described
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: acquisition_methods and collection_mechanisms populated; distribution_formats populated and an access route documented
sub_elements.evidence: collection_mechanisms: five entries - sites create and upload a CHoRUS Data Extract using the chorus-extract-upload tooling following an interactive workflow diagram linked to validated SOPs; bedside monitors with gateway/middleware supply telemetry; imaging drawn from PACS; EEG drawn from hospital EEG databases in EDF+ and Persyst; notes extracted and tokenized with the OHNLP toolkit
sub_elements.quality_note: One mechanism per modality, each naming the system it comes from and the tooling that moves it. The submission workflow is described concretely enough that a contributing site could follow it.

sub_elements.name: Data Acquisition Methods Listed
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: same condition as above
sub_elements.evidence: acquisition_methods: three entries flagged was_directly_observed, was_inferred_derived and was_validated_verified, covering retrospective capture during care (including medication administration time-stamped at each infusion change), derivation via tokenization and OMOP standardisation, and validation of semantic mappings and SOPs; raw_data_sources: five entries with native formats
sub_elements.quality_note: The acquisition flags are used correctly rather than all set true, and the derived entry explains precisely why delivered records differ from site source records. Raw sources are listed separately with their pre-standardisation formats.

sub_elements.name: Preprocessing, Cleaning, Labeling, and Annotation Quality
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: external_resources references a code repository: 'https://github.com/chorus-ai - the CHoRUS for Equitable AI GitHub organization, holding 28 repositories including chorus-extract-upload, Chorus_SOP, ... chorus_waveform ...'
sub_elements.evidence: preprocessing_strategies: three entries (OMOP standardisation via validated semantic mappings maintained in chorus-mapping; extraction and tokenization of unstructured text with the OHNLP toolkit plus transformation limiting re-identification; waveform conversion using the scripts in chorus_waveform with supporting chorus_waveform_resources); cleaning_strategies: characterization reports returned to sites via CHoRUSReports, and validated mappings with a clinical validation SOP; labeling_strategies: the planned annotation environment, caveated as future tense
sub_elements.quality_note: Preprocessing is documented per modality and tied to the repository that holds the code for each step. Cleaning includes a real feedback loop to contributing sites. Labeling is honestly marked as not yet present in the release. No annotation_analyses, machine_annotation_tools or imputation_protocols, consistent with a release that carries no labels yet.

sub_elements.name: Software and Tools Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Under the quoted rule (#1079): the dataset was processed, established from Element 8's collection and preprocessing fields, which are populated with a per-modality processing chain. Under my own definition's repository gate the condition is also met via external_resources naming github.com/chorus-ai and 28 repositories. Both give applicable.
sub_elements.evidence: preprocessing_strategies prose names the processing software: the chorus-mapping repository holding the pooled tabular mappings used for OMOP standardisation; the OHNLP toolkit used to extract and tokenize note text; and 'the conversion scripts and documentation maintained in the chorus_waveform repository' used to convert waveform data for release. is_deidentified.deidentification_details additionally names a privacy scan tool and a CTP-deid repository. external_resources corroborates by naming those repositories inside the chorus-ai organisation.
sub_elements.quality_note: Slot carrying the evidence: preprocessing_strategies prose, corroborated by is_deidentified.deidentification_details and external_resources. There is no software_and_tools slot, but the sub-element asks whether a reader can tell what software produced or processed the data being distributed, and here they can, per modality: chorus-mapping for the 1.6 billion released OMOP rows, the OHNLP toolkit for the released tokens, chorus_waveform for the released 23 Tb of waveforms. None of the three exclusions applies. (a) fails: processing software is named. (b) fails: these are processing tools, not capture or hosting; the bedside monitors and PACS are named separately in collection slots and are not what carries this point. (c) fails: the waveform entry says conversion is 'for release' and the corresponding volume is reported as released, and the OMOP and tokenized-note outputs are likewise in the release. The labeling pipeline is the one whose outputs are not in the release, and it is not the basis for this score. No version numbers are given for any tool, which weakens the evidence without taking the point under the quoted threshold.

sub_elements.name: External Standards and Resources Referenced
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: distribution_formats populated and an access route documented
sub_elements.evidence: external_resources: the chorus-ai GitHub organisation with 28 named repositories, chorus4ai.org with its page inventory, the NIH RePORTER award record, and the AIM-AHEAD cohort-2 informational webinar PDF; conforms_to naming OMOP, DICOM, WFDB, EDF+, Persyst and the OHNLP open source schema
sub_elements.quality_note: Standards and documentation are both referenced, each annotated with what it contains and why it matters. The webinar and RePORTER links are the evidentiary basis for several figures elsewhere in the record, so the linkage is functional rather than decorative.

elements.name: Dataset Evaluation and Limitations Disclosure
elements.description: Does the metadata communicate known risks, biases, or dataset limitations?

sub_elements.name: Known Limitations Documented
sub_elements.evidence: known_limitations: four typed entries - coverage_limitation (imaging limited to about 1,000 images, EEG extraction in process), integration_limitation (note text not co-located, only tokens in the enclave), representativeness_limitation (14 of 20 centres, achieved distribution not reported), scope_limitation (ICU/PICU/NICU only); the coverage entry carries a scope_impact stating that analyses needing imaging or EEG at scale are not yet supported
sub_elements.quality_note: Limitations are typed, specific and consequential, and at least one states what it prevents a reuser from doing. This is the strongest part of Element 9.

sub_elements.name: Biases Categorized Using Standard Taxonomy (RAI-aligned)
sub_elements.evidence: no known_biases slot; no future_use_impacts slot; the representativeness_limitation entry notes only that the achieved distribution is not reported
sub_elements.quality_note: No structured bias categorisation and no BiasTypeEnum values, in a multi-site critical-care dataset where selection and site-mix bias are foreseeable. Anticipated downstream social impacts are likewise not recorded, although the project's own materials frame equity as a goal.

sub_elements.name: Data Anomalies and Quality Issues Noted
sub_elements.evidence: no anomalies slot; data quality content appears only as coverage gaps in known_limitations and as source-document discrepancies in the top-level source_caveats
sub_elements.quality_note: The discrepancies documented are between the sources describing the dataset (50,000 versus over 45K admissions, 7,642 admissions versus 1000 images, a partially separated table in the extracted text), not anomalies within the data. Nothing on outliers, artefacts, monitor dropouts, mapping failures or missing-value rates in the released records.

sub_elements.name: Sensitive Content and Warnings Provided
sub_elements.evidence: sensitive_elements.sensitivity_details enumerating demographics, diagnoses, procedures, medication administration, nursing flowsheets, notes, imaging, telemetry, EEG, social determinants of health and geographic distance to the nearest hospital, and stating that every data type in the inventory is under controlled access; confidential_elements recording that note text is not releasable
sub_elements.quality_note: Sensitivity is enumerated at the level of the specific elements present, including the re-identifying combination of social determinants and geographic distance, and is paired with the access control that answers it. No content_warnings slot, which matters little here since the sensitivity statement carries the warning.

sub_elements.name: Ethical Review Details Including Conflicts
sub_elements.evidence: ethical_reviews.review_details describing the Ethical and Trustworthy AI pillar, community-facing ethics focus groups determining what data is appropriate for public sharing, evaluation of community perspectives on clinical care AI, a legal framework for collecting data at scale, and analysis of the legal and regulatory landscape
sub_elements.quality_note: Substantive, specific ethical-review documentation that describes actual activities rather than a compliance assertion. No conflict-of-interest disclosure, and no named board or determination, which is the same gap raised as a consistency issue under Element 4 and is not charged twice here.

elements.name: Cross-Platform and Community Integration
elements.description: Does the dataset connect to wider data ecosystems, repositories, or standards?
elements.applicability_note: Datasets shared and available for reuse: CONDITION MET. Publication identified (gating sub-element 2): borderline. There is no citation slot and no publication DOI or PMID; external_resources carries an NIH RePORTER award record and an AIM-AHEAD webinar PDF, which are published documents but not scholarly publication references. Under the ambiguity rule the borderline case defaults to applicable, so sub-element 2 is scored rather than excluded, and no sub-element is excluded from the denominator.

sub_elements.name: Dataset Published on a Recognized Platform
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: distribution_formats populated with five formats; documented access route
sub_elements.evidence: no publisher slot; the data are described as held in the Bridge2AI AI/ML for Clinical Care Collaborative Cloud enclave with CHoRUS services deployed on Azure, with notes kept locally at contributing sites
sub_elements.quality_note: No publishing repository is named. The enclave is an access environment, not a recognised data repository with its own identifier and deposit record, and it is described in a distribution note rather than a publisher field.

sub_elements.name: Citation and DOI for Cross-referencing
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met. Publication condition is borderline: external_resources includes the NIH RePORTER record and a published AIM-AHEAD webinar PDF, but no scholarly publication and no citation slot. Ambiguity rule applied, so this is scored rather than excluded, to avoid silent N/A inflation.
sub_elements.evidence: no citation slot; no doi slot
sub_elements.quality_note: No recommended citation and no DOI, so there is no way to credit or cross-reference the dataset itself. This compounds the missing persistent identifier in Element 1: a paper using these data has nothing stable to cite.

sub_elements.name: Community Standards or Schema Conformance
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: same datasets-shared condition
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to_standard: [OMOP_CDM, DICOM, WFDB, OTHER]; conforms_to prose mapping each modality to OMOP, DICOM, WFDB, EDF+/Persyst and the OHNLP open source schema; per-collection conforms_to values inside all five file_collections
sub_elements.quality_note: Community standard adoption is the record's strongest integration claim and is stated consistently in three places, including where a standard is extended rather than used as published.

sub_elements.name: Outreach Materials and Documentation Links
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: same datasets-shared condition
sub_elements.evidence: external_resources listing chorus4ai.org pages on team, project overview, tools, data acquisition, standards, community engagement, ethics, the dataset and learning resources, plus the AIM-AHEAD cohort-2 informational webinar PDF; extension_mechanism.contribution_url: https://github.com/chorus-ai with a developer web guide in the chorus-developer repository and Standards and Data Acquisition discussion spaces
sub_elements.quality_note: Documentation, training material and contribution routes are all linked, including how an outside collaborator would join the mapping effort. This is genuine community-facing outreach rather than a bare homepage.

sub_elements.name: Related Datasets with Typed Relationships
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: same datasets-shared condition
sub_elements.evidence: no related_datasets slot
sub_elements.quality_note: No related dataset is recorded with any relationship type, even though the record names the other Bridge2AI data generation projects in purposes and describes a planned holdout partition of its own data.

strengths: Modality-by-modality standards documentation that stays consistent across four separate slots, mapping structured EHR to OMOP, imaging to DICOM, telemetry to WFDB, EEG to EDF+ and Persyst, and notes to the OHNLP schema, and stating where a standard is extended rather than used as published

A traceable processing chain from hospital source system through native format to released format, with the code repository for each step named in preprocessing prose (chorus-mapping, the OHNLP toolkit, chorus_waveform) so a reader can tell what produced the data being distributed

Disciplined separation of released from planned throughout: the holdout test set, the annotation environment, the sampling approach and the imaging and EEG completion states each carry a caveat marking them as intentions rather than delivered artefacts

Funding transparency that validates on inspection: an NIH grant number in correct activity-institute-serial form, cross-checked against both the project website and the RePORTER record, with award amount, application ID and a project period consistent with the reported snapshot date

Honest treatment of conflicting sources rather than silent reconciliation, recording both the 50,000 and the over-45K cohort figures, explaining that the two imaging figures are different units, and naming the manifest precedence rule that decided which figure was recorded
weaknesses: No persistent identifier, no DOI and no recommended citation, so the dataset cannot be cited or cross-referenced; the id slot merely repeats the project homepage that also fills the landing-page slot

No version, no version access method and no errata, in a dataset the record itself describes as partially released and actively growing from 50,000 toward 100,000 admissions, which leaves an analysis unable to state what it was run against

Consent is entirely undocumented although human subject involvement is asserted, with neither a consent procedure nor the IRB waiver that retrospective record research would normally rest on, and no IRB or ethics committee of record for the dataset

No variable-level metadata, no data dictionary and no tabular flag, despite 1.6 billion rows of structured data being the largest component, and no statement of which OMOP tables or CDM version are populated

No bias categorisation and no anomalies documentation, so a multi-site critical-care dataset with a stated equity goal records neither its foreseeable selection and site-mix biases nor any quality defect inside the released records
recommendations: Mint a DOI for the released cohort and add a recommended citation, then give the id slot a value distinct from the landing page so the dataset is separable from the project website
Add a version for the current release with a version_access statement describing how a prior snapshot can be obtained, and start an errata or change log keyed to those versions

Record the IRB or reliance agreement of record with its approval identifier, and add an informed_consent entry stating either the consent mechanism or the waiver under which retrospective records were released

Add known_biases with structured categories covering site selection, the 14-of-20-centre contribution mix and the ICU/PICU/NICU setting restriction, and add anomalies covering monitor dropouts, mapping failures and missing-value rates in the released data
Add variables with the OMOP tables and CDM version populated and an is_tabular flag, and add prohibited_uses or discouraged_uses to complete the reuse guidance for identifiable critical-care data
